prompt:
Make ONE strictly localized painting correction to this exact transparent character cutout: repaint ONLY THE VIOLET FABRIC'S LIGHT AND SHADOW GROUPING. Preserve the identical character design, face, hair, anatomy, pose, garment construction, folds' structural positions, gold trim, armor, bow, arrow, hands, saturated palette, framing and alpha cutout. Do not add or remove clothing, ornament or limbs. Retain true transparent background and all transparent gaps.
The current violet sleeves, torso and skirt are broken up into many disconnected lavender and dark-purple polygon patches. These look like faded or damaged fabric. Replace those fragmented patches with a clean cohesive matte fabric treatment. Establish one uninterrupted, rich royal-violet base color across each continuous garment panel. Use only two or three closely related value families, with ONE broad connected shadow mass on the underside of each larger form, instead of separately lighting every crease. Preserve believable overall round volume with gentle transitions over large forms. A few necessary folds at the elbow, waist belt, hip and skirt attachment should follow actual tension and compression; keep their shadows joined to the main shadow where appropriate. The upper sleeve should read as one rounded tube with an underside shadow and a small number of meaningful elbow folds. The fitted torso should read as one connected cloth surface from chest through waist, with broad coherent light direction and no separate pale patches on each bulge. The overskirt should read as complete flowing fabric panels whose larger fold shadows extend from the belt and hip to the hem, not a mosaic of triangulated color islands.
Keep the base purple saturated and consistent. Remove arbitrary light-purple islands, triangular faceting, mottled patches, patchwork hue shifts, little streak highlights, faded edges, paint chips, tiny wrinkle shading and spotty texture. No new stripes or gradients crossing garment construction. Highlights should be soft, sparse and close to the local purple, never chalky white or pink. Do not flatten the figure into a featureless silhouette: maintain the few large structural shadows required to show the actual body and cloth overlap. Treat fabric as matte woven cloth, not faceted metal or crumpled paper. Leave metallic gold regions and every non-fabric element as they are. SAME drawing and pose, refined coherent cloth values only. Output PNG with actual alpha transparency, no added backdrop, no glow, no checkerboard painted into pixels, no ground or cast shadow, no text.
